text:
Anya: Heads-up — I'm drafting a short PRD for "customer evidence bundles" for private/VPC customers who request SOC2/ISO artifacts. Want alignment on what goes in the bundle, redaction rules, delivery options, and minimal acceptance criteria. Putting rough ideas here.

Sam: +1. We need to avoid handing over raw PHI/PII and keep the artifacts scoped to what auditors actually need. Prefer attestations + sampled artifacts, not full raw streams.

Mike: Can we make bundle generation fully automated? Idea: async export job that snapshots relevant metadata and pulls sampled log segments, then zips and signs. Should be non-blocking for serving.

Lee: Implementation notes from infra: bundles must be encrypted at rest, and we should support either (a) wrap with customer CMK (if private has customer KMS) or (b) redact & encrypt with Redwood-managed key. HSM integration can be optional later. Also we need rate limits for bundle generation jobs.

Rachel: Legal: we need a documented request flow and consent for sharing customer-adjacent logs. Also a redaction checklist (IP, PII, credentials). We should define retention of delivered bundles (e.g., 90d by default) and a delete/recall process.

Anya: Draft acceptance criteria (MVP):
```
- bundle manifest (manifest.json) listing artifacts + hashes + generation metadata
- config snapshot (model config, runtime config, deployed model version)
- sampled request/response pairs (redacted) with sampling rationale
- sidecar traces and shard-level metrics (aggregated)
- access control log for who generated/downloaded the bundle
- delivery via time-limited secure link (S3 presigned or private portal)
- every artifact hashed and signature-attested by our build key
- privacy filter applied before bundle creation (PII/keys removed)
```
These should satisfy basic SOC2 evidence requests and be useful for ISO audits.

Sam: A couple of edge cases: 1) customer asks for full raw logs — we should require an escalation + legal sign-off and a narrow TTL. 2) multi-tenant traces that overlap other customers — must ensure strict tenant isolation and no cross-tenant artifacts.

Mike: Engineering constraints: generating large bundles from hot nodes may impact perf. Proposal: snapshot metadata + request caches, then stream logs from cold storage. For immediate needs, offer a fast-sampled mode (<5 min) and a deep-export mode (hours).

Lee: Ops checklist: define per-tenant export quotas, idempotency keys for re-runs, and an audit event emitted to our central telemetry pipeline when a bundle is created or accessed. Also add encryption envelope headers in manifest so customers can verify CMK wrapping.

Rachel: Compliance ask: add a mapping doc that ties each artifact in the bundle to the control(s) it supports (SOC2/ISO IDs). We'll need that for gate reviews.

Anya: Proposed roll plan for MVP:
- Week 0: agree on artifact list + redaction rules + legal sign-off on request flow
- Week 1–2: eng spike for async export job + manifest format
- Week 3: infra work for key wrapping + secure delivery endpoint
- Week 4: internal QA + one pilot customer export
- Gate: compliance sign-off + product acceptance checklist (see criteria above)

Sam: Suggest we add an acceptance test: generate bundle, run redaction scanner (automated), verify manifest hashes, and confirm access logs show only approved users.

Mike: Implementation note: sample manifest skeleton:
```json
{
  "bundle_id": "uuid",
  "generated_by": "username",
  "generated_at": "iso_ts",
  "encryption": { "mode": "cmk", "wrapped": true },
  "artifacts": [ { "name":"config.json","sha256":"..." }, ... ]
}
```
We can keep this small and version it.

Anya: Questions for the group: 1) any objections to the artifact list above? 2) is CMK-first wrapping feasible for Private customers (Lee)? 3) legal ok with redaction scope (Rachel)?

Lee: CMK-first is feasible if customer provides KMS access/we'll implement dual-wrap for escrow. For on-prem air-gapped installs, we may surface an offline packaging tool.

Rachel: Redaction scope: ok for MVP as long as we maintain an escalation path. We'll draft a short consent template for the request UI.

Sam: I'll start a SOC2/ISO crosswalk doc mapping artifacts to controls and share a link here.

prod-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/redwood/evb-2024-03 (draft) :white_check_mark:

Anya: Great — thanks all. I'll turn this thread into a one-pager PRD and post the RFC link. Please add any last comments in the next 24h so I can lock scope for the spike.
